profile.objective:
Comprehensive Knowledge and Skills: Acquire comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in computing, enabling them to excel in diverse careers and adapt to the evolving demands of the industry.
Lifelong Learning: Develop a mindset of lifelong learning, continuously enhancing their knowledge and skills to stay relevant in the fast-paced technological landscape.
Innovation and Problem-Solving: Engage in innovative practices that address real-world technological challenges, contributing to advancements in the field of computer applications.
Entrepreneurial Thinking and Leadership: Cultivate entrepreneurial thinking and leadership qualities, empowering them to take initiative in shaping the digital landscape and developing impactful technological solutions.

courses.outcomes:

modules.title: List ADT
modules.revised: Data Structures - Types - List ADT, Implementation using Arrays, Singly Linked List, Doubly Linked List- all operations (Creation, Insertion, Deletion, Search and Traversal), Circular Linked Lists, Applications of Linked Lists-Polynomial addition and subtraction - Sparse Matrix Implementation.

modules.title: Stack & Queue ADT
modules.revised:
Stack ADT: Stack using Array, Stack using Linked List, applications of Stacks, Balancing Symbols, conversion of infix to postfix expression - Evaluating arithmetic expressions.
Queue ADT: Queue implementation using Array, Queue implementation using Linked List, applications of Queue, Priority Queue — Circular Queue and Queue Applications.

modules.title: Trees ADT
modules.revised: Introduction - Tree Terminologies - Binary Tree ADT - Binary Tree Traversals: Pre-order, In-order & Post-order - Expression Trees - Binary Search Tree ADT & operations - AVL Trees - Heaps & Types - Introduction to B & B+ Trees.

modules.title: Hashing & Graphs ADT
modules.revised:
Hashing - Hashing functions - Collision Strategies - Separate Chaining - Open Addressing: Linear Probing - Quadratic Probing - Double Hashing.
Graphs ADT: Introduction - Terminologies - Graphs Types - Graphs Representation Techniques - BFS & DFS Traversal Techniques.

modules.title: Sorting and Searching Algorithms

courses.outcomes:

modules.title: Introduction to Computer Networks
modules.revised: Overview of Computer Networks - Types of Networks: LAN, WAN, MAN, and PAN - Network Topologies: Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, Hybrid - OSI and TCP/IP Models - Network Devices: Routers, Switches, Hubs, and Bridges - Data Transmission: Analog vs. Digital Signals - Bandwidth and Throughput.

modules.title: Network Protocols and Communication

modules.title: Routing and Switching

modules.title: Network Security and Management

courses.outcomes:
Explain the scope, limitations, and applications of AI.
Apply advanced search techniques to solve state-space problems.
Develop reasoning systems using logical representation and inference techniques.

modules.title: Introduction to AI

modules.title: List of experiments
modules.revised:
1. Write a program to create Employees Database using Singly Linked List with following fields in a node: Employee ID Name Salary Operations: a) Insert employee data b) Display the entire List c) Search for the salary of given employee id.
2. Write a program to create Students Database using Doubly Linked List with following fields in a node: Student USN Name CGPA Operations: a) Insert students data b) Display the entire List (Forward & Backward) c) Search for the CGPA of given student’s usn.
3. Demonstrate the working principle of Stack ADT using Arrays and Linked List.
4. Write a program that uses stack operations to convert a given infix expression into its postfix equivalent.
5. Demonstrate the working principle of Queue ADT using Arrays and Linked List.
6. Write a program to demonstrate Circular Queue using Array.
7. Write a program to create an Expression Tree for an arithmetic expression: Operations: i) Infix expression - Inorder Traversal ii) Prefix expression - Preorder Traversal iii) Postfix expression - Postorder Traversal
8. Write a program to create a Binary Search Tree for the Customer Database using the following fields. Customer ID Customer Name Customer Purchase Capacity Operations: i) Insert Customer Data ii) Searching for Customer details who has maximum purchase capacity iii) Searching for Customer details who has minimum purchase capacity
9. Write program for demonstrating Hashing technique with Searching operation and Linear Probing Collision Strategy. 10.Write programs for implementing the Graphs Traversal Techniques. a) Breadth first graph traversal b) Depth first graph traversal 11.Write programs for following sorting techniques. a) Insertion Sort b) Quick Sort 12.Write programs for following searching algorithms. a) Linear Search b) Binary Search using Array

notes: Course codes starting with TBA- are placeholders: the matrices leave the code blank for the open electives, the Trans Disciplinary Project Centric Learning courses and the semester-4 Project / Internship. Replace them with the codes the university assigns.

TD-PCL-1, TD-PCL-2 and Research Methodology are listed twice in the matrices — once with 0 credits in the semester they start and once with their credits in the semester they finish. They are imported once, in the credited semester.
Elective pairs are kept as one row with both codes and titles separated by “ / ”, as in the matrices. Each option gets its own syllabus.
CA and ESE are imported as the percentage weightages printed in the matrices (out of 100); “NA” is imported as 0.

MCACYS (Cyber Security): the course-code column of 2026-2028_MCA_CS_Course Matrix.xlsx is shifted against the titles in semesters I and III. Semester I–II core codes are taken from the other four MCA matrices (same titles); semester III codes follow the CS syllabus. 25MCACS302 / 25MCACS302L (Applied Cryptography), 25CSPGET11 / 25CSPGEP11, 25MCACRM1 and 25MCACS304SI / 25MCACS304CP are inferred from the numbering — confirm them.

MCAISM (ISMS): semester II row 4 repeats the lab code “25MCAISE2041L / 25MCAISE2042L” for the theory electives; imported as 25MCAISE2041 / 25MCAISE2042 (Ethical Hacking / Network Security), matching the ISMS syllabus.
MCASCT (Storage and Cloud Technology): the internship code “25MCAIS304SI / 25MCAIS304CP” is the ISMS code in the source matrix. Imported as written — confirm it.
MCAREG and MCASCT: the semester-2 TD-PCL row is titled “Transdisciplinary Project Centric Learning 2” in the matrix; imported as TD-PCL-1 (the course started in semester 1).

MCAIML (AIML): there is no AIML syllabus in the Drive folder. The courses AIML shares with MCA General (same code and title) take their syllabus from MCA_GEN_SYLLABUS_2026_28.docx; the AIML specialisation courses still need a syllabus.

BCAGAI (BCA Generative AI): the folder has the minor buckets and the Generative AI syllabus, but no BCA course matrix. The minors are imported into Annexure I and the syllabi are imported without course codes; the programme structure still has to be entered. The degree level is set to UG - 4 Year (Honours with Research) from the eight-semester folder — change it if needed.
BCA minors: 26BCAIH6MR01 (Edge Computing, IoT minor) and 26BCAIH4MR02L (Software Architecture lab) repeat Healthcare-minor codes in the source workbook. Imported as written.

The Drive files are attached as the department would upload them: each course matrix in its programme's Curriculum (the BCA minor buckets for BCAGAI), each syllabus document in its programme's Syllabus, and the checklist and articulation sheets kept on this page. A file that is not in app/pack_data/files/csit/ is listed as missing on loading; add it there and press Load again.
